selected.family: one read-only multi-statement transaction with stable snapshot semantics
selected.implementation_form: private raw node-postgres PoolClient helper inside PostgresAuthorizationRepository
selected.transaction_start: BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY
rationale: PostgreSQL 17 Repeatable Read pins one snapshot at the first non-transaction-control statement and successive SELECTs see that same snapshot.
Read-only Repeatable Read transactions do not incur serialization conflicts from concurrent updates.
node-postgres requires every transaction statement to use the same checked-out client; the repository already owns a pg Pool and already uses explicit transactions for mutations.
This reuses existing SELECTs, mappers, precedence and management bulk-loading logic instead of replacing them with two complex aggregate SQL shapes.

primitive_boundary.name: private repository read-snapshot helper (exact identifier left to implementation)
behavior: pool.connect() exactly once per composite read
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY on that client
route every component query for the composite result through that same PoolClient
COMMIT only after result construction succeeds
on an operation or COMMIT failure, best-effort ROLLBACK when a transaction began, while preserving the original operation/commit error as primary
do not translate database errors inside the primitive; existing Hyperdrive availability classifier remains the only translation boundary
primitive_boundary.public_api: No public repository/service/capability signature or response shape change. Existing resolveUser optional Queryable path, if retained for compatibility, must be treated only as an already-bound internal database context; normal one-argument service/capability resolution enters the snapshot helper.

query_routing.resolveUser: role/assignment, role-grant and override reads use the same snapshot client; missing-user discrimination must also remain on that same client if reached
query_routing.management: roles, users/assignments, grants and overrides use the same snapshot client; data-query count remains four
query_routing.unaffected: single-statement hasPermission, ordinary list/read helpers and all mutations remain outside this composite read helper unless a current R7 contract requires otherwise

rejected.reason: PostgreSQL gives each SELECT a fresh statement snapshot at READ COMMITTED, so it does not satisfy TC-08-B.

rejected.family: single SQL statement/CTE per composite operation
reason: One PostgreSQL statement would inherently use one statement snapshot.
resolveUser and management state would each require bespoke aggregation/JSON/query mapping, duplicating or relocating current precedence and response assembly.
The management query is materially more complex and raises larger review/regression risk than wrapping the existing four bounded reads.
It provides no shared primitive between REM-10 and REM-11 beyond a general design idea.

rejected.status: viable implementation of the transaction family but not selected
rejected.reason: Drizzle supports repeatable-read/read-only config, but this repository is currently raw pg; introducing a Drizzle database wrapper solely for R7 is broader than a private PoolClient helper.
The contract requires one stable read snapshot, not serializable conflict detection; Repeatable Read read-only already provides the required stable view with less unnecessary machinery.

delivery_topology.decision: one standalone R7 implementation PR covering REM-10 and REM-11
rationale: Both units modify the same authorization repository and are best served by one shared private snapshot primitive.
REM-11 is recommended after REM-10 for reuse/review clarity, and separate logical commits inside one PR preserve that sequencing without duplicate shared-file churn.

PROJECT_STATE currently records one limitation covering both contracts and must not declare R7 resolved after only one unit; one PR allows one final factual-state transition after both are implemented.
The units remain independently testable through separate deterministic database regressions.
